scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2023, ZEEKR delivered a total of 196,633 ZEEKR vehicles since first delivery in October 2021, including 192,441 delivered in China.
scores.M_value: 1 manufacturer matched: 'ZEEKR INTELLIGENT TECHNOLOGY US, LLC', country CHINA, vehicle_types=['Passenger Car']. NHTSA confirms Zeekr is a registered passenger-car OEM but carries no delivery-volume data.
scores.interpretation: NHTSA vPIC covers US-sold vehicles ONLY. 192,441 of the 196,633 cumulative deliveries were in China, which no US federal registry records. Per the foreign-private-issuer caveat, absence of China-market delivery volume in a US registry is NOT a contradiction. The registry does affirmatively corroborate that Zeekr is a real, registered passenger-car manufacturer (not a glider/incomplete-vehicle shell, unlike the Lordstown pattern). The specific cumulative volume claim is not testable against any available registry -> UNVERIFIABLE (OEM-existence corroborated; volume firewalled by sector/registry mismatch).

scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2023, ZEEKR had 1,258 patents (including 123 invention patents) and 2,465 pending patent applications.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=3, n_granted=0. The 3 US applications (Vehicle Trunk Lid, Automobile, Vehicle light) were all filed Apr-May 2024 (after FY2023), assignee 'Zhejiang Zeekr Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd' — design/utility filings, none granted pre-cutoff.
scores.interpretation: USPTO ODP indexes US patent filings only. A Chinese BEV maker's 1,258-patent portfolio is overwhelmingly filed with CNIPA (China), not USPTO; the filing itself describes the patents as Chinese-jurisdiction IP. USPTO showing ~0 is the EXPECTED foreign-issuer pattern, NOT the Nikola red-flag pattern (Nikola requires the registry to COVER the claimed tech area and show near-zero). USPTO does not cover China-filed patents, so it cannot ground-truth this claim. Absence in USPTO for a China-domiciled patent portfolio is not a contradiction -> UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: ZEEKR announced a plan to integrate NVIDIA DRIVE Thor, the 2,000 TOPS AV superchip, into its centralized vehicle computer for its next generation intelligent BEV.
scores.M_value: 3 NVIDIA-filed hits mentioning Zeekr: 8-K 2022-11-16 (q3fy23 PR), 8-K 2024-02-21 (q4fy24 PR), and NVIDIA's 10-K filed 2024-02-21 (nvda-20240128). NVIDIA discloses Zeekr in its own annual report and earnings releases.
scores.interpretation: The counterparty (NVIDIA) independently and repeatedly discloses the Zeekr relationship in its own SEC filings, including its 10-K. This is direct counterparty corroboration of the DRIVE Thor / AV-compute partnership at materiality cadence (earnings-release + annual-report level). Although the integration itself is forward ('next generation'), the named-partner relationship is registry-corroborated by the partner -> PASS.

scores.claim_text: ZEEKR deploys cutting-edge autonomous driving technology by world-leading players such as Mobileye into its BEVs.
scores.M_value: 34 total external hits; the top hits are Mobileye Global Inc. (MBLY) 8-Ks dated 2023-01-26, 2023-04-27, and 2023-10-26 (earnings-release exhibits) each naming Zeekr. Mobileye independently and recurrently discloses Zeekr in its own SEC filings.
scores.interpretation: Mobileye, the named ADAS/AV partner, discloses the Zeekr relationship across multiple of its own quarterly 8-K earnings exhibits — recurring counterparty corroboration well above the SUB_MATERIAL threshold. The vendor relationship is independently verified -> PASS.

scores.claim_text: ZEEKR equips its vehicles with CATL's Qilin battery; ZEEKR 009 was the first mass-produced BEV model equipped with CATL's Qilin battery.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Zeekr', all filers) — used to scan for counterparty (CATL) disclosure
scores.M_value: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology) is a Shenzhen-listed Chinese battery maker and is NOT a SEC reporter, so it does not appear as a corroborating filer. The 34-hit external corpus corroborates the Zeekr ecosystem broadly (NVIDIA, Mobileye, Visteon, Navitas) but contains no CATL-side SEC disclosure because CATL files no US reports.
scores.interpretation: No US federal registry covers a China-to-China battery-supply arrangement, and the named supplier (CATL) is not an SEC filer, so counterparty-disclosure is structurally unavailable. Absence is not a contradiction. The claim is internally specific and consistent with the broadly-corroborated Zeekr supply ecosystem, but no independent registry can ground-truth it -> UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: ZEEKR vehicles are manufactured at Geely-owned plants; Geely Holding was ZEEKR's largest supplier for 2022 and 2023, with vehicle purchases of RMB18.6B (2022) and RMB25.6B (2023).
scores.M_value: going_concern detector returned signal=NOT_FOUND_FILING (no 10-K/10-Q exists for the CIK — ZEEKR is a foreign private issuer that files F-1/20-F, not domestic 10-K). Related-party note discloses RMB1,626.0M / 18,605.1M / 25,550.7M vehicle purchases from Geely (2021/22/23) plus SEA license and three factory cooperation framework agreements — fully and consistently disclosed in the prospectus.
scores.interpretation: Geely is a Hong-Kong/China-listed related party, not an SEC filer; no US registry (EPA/NHTSA/USAspending) covers Chinese OEM manufacturing arrangements. The going-concern detector is inapplicable to a foreign filer with no domestic 10-K. The intercompany manufacturing/supply relationship is the company's central disclosed dependency and is detailed self-consistently across the related-party and contractual-obligations notes, but it cannot be independently registry-verified -> UNVERIFIABLE (no benign-vs-adverse signal available; absence is structural, not suspicious).

scores.claim_text: ZEEKR had 16,645 employees as of December 31, 2023 (15,859 in mainland China, 786 in Europe), including a Sweden-based R&D center (CEVT).
scores.M_value: 0 hits for 'CEVT' across all SEC filers. CEVT (China Euro Vehicle Technology AB) is a privately-held Swedish R&D subsidiary; it is not an SEC reporter and is not separately disclosed by any SEC filer. No US workforce registry (OSHA 300A / DOL H-1B LCA) covers China- or Sweden-based headcount.
scores.interpretation: The workforce is entirely China- and Europe-based; no US employment registry covers it, and the Swedish R&D entity files nothing with the SEC. Absence of CEVT in EDGAR is the expected foreign-operations pattern, not a contradiction. The headcount claim is not testable against any available US registry -> UNVERIFIABLE.
